Author: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Bench: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
 Office Notes,

Sl. or proceedings
 Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order

S No or directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  WPMS 2280/2024  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Darshan Singh, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. Devendra Pant, Standing Counsel, for the State.
Mr. Naresh Pant, Advocate, for the NHAI.
Mr. Manoj Kumar, Standing Counsel, for the Union of India.
(2) This writ petition has been filed by petitioner on behalf of Vedmata Gayatri Trust, Halduchaur, Nainital.

According to petitioner, a plot of land was leased out in favour of Vedmata Gayatri Trust, Halduchaur for a period of 30 years w.e.f.
23.8.2006 and a temple and ashram were constructed over the said land.
It is further his case that a portion of the temple and ashram were demolished by National Highways Authority of India while constructing National Highway.
According to petitioner, a meagre amount of 1,05,907/- was paid as compensation in respect of the building which was demolished.

In this writ petition, petitioner has sought the following reliefs:
"I. Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding and directing the respondents no. to pay the compensation under the "Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act- 2013" in view of the fact that 610 square meters of land has been acquired by the NHAI of the petitioner's trust, from the 0.145 hectare land in khet/khasara no. 464 area 0.623 hectare of Khatauni number 113 of village Jaggibungar tehsil Lalkuan, district Nainital, to the four times of the market value of the land acquired, along with specified interest as stipulated under the Act.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act- 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Or;
II. Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding and directing the respondents i.e., Competent Authority/Special Land Acquisition Officer Nainital/U.S. Nagar and NHAI Rudrapur to adjudicate/decide the compensation a fresh by adjudicating the issue keeping in view of the fact that the land in question was recorded as leased land on the date of acquisition and WPMS/2280/2024 on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55999463/
1 notification issued u/s 3-D and 3-G of the National Highways Act 1956.
III. Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari to quashing the Award dated 02.08.2016, passed by the Competent Authority/Special Land Acquisition Officer Nainital/U.S. Nagar only to the extent that whereby in the Sl.
No.6 Survey no. 464 has been mentioned as government land in the revenue record and further to modify/correct the award dated 02.8.2016 accordingly.
IV. Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari to quashing the communication dated 19.12.2023 (Annexure no.7) whereby compensation has been denied to the trust of the petitioner in the letter sent by the Manager (Technical)
through Project Director NHAI Rudrapur to the Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Nainital, as well as the communication dated 20.02.2024 made to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Nainital (Annexure no.9) V. Issue a suitable writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to compensate for the actual damage caused to the housing structures, temples, ashram/building etc. of the trust of the petitioner by conducting re-surveys of the spot."
(3) Learned Counsel for the respondents contended that since the land, in question,
is government land and is leased out in favour of petitioner for a limited period,
therefore, petitioner is not entitled for compensation in respect of the said land.
(4) Learned Counsel for the petitioner, however, refers to a communication dated 29.12.2023, issued by Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Nainital to the Project Director, National Highways Authority.
In the said letter, in the last sentence of the first paragraph, it is observed that Vedmata Gayatri Trust is entitled to compensation as a lease deed was executed in its favour.

(5) Since the Special Land Acquisition Officer has expressed the opinion that the Vedmata Gayatri Trust is entitled to compensation even for the leased land,
therefore, the writ petition is disposed of by directing Special Land Acquisition Officer, Nainital/Competent Authority, Land Acquisition to decide the issue of compensation, if payable for the leased land, to Vedmata Gayatri Trust, as per law,
within six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 9.9.2024 Pr WPMS/2280/2024 on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55999463/
